short.q: Explain why a Unicode text file is usually larger than the same text stored in ASCII.
short.model: Unicode uses more bits per character (up to 32) so that it can represent many more characters. ASCII uses only 7 or 8 bits, so the same number of characters needs fewer bits.
points: Unicode uses more bits per character
so the same text needs more storage than ASCII

short.q: A bitmap is 100 pixels wide and 50 pixels high with a colour depth of 16 bits. Calculate its file size in bytes.
State two effects of increasing the resolution of an image.
short.model: The image has more detail and looks sharper, but the file size becomes larger because there are more pixels to store.

short.q: Compress WWWWBBWWWWWW with run-length encoding and explain whether it is lossless or lossy.
short.model: 4W2B6W. It is lossless because the original data can be rebuilt exactly from the encoded form.
points: lossless as original can be restored exactly

short.q: Explain why data is encrypted before it is sent across a network.
short.model: So that if the data is intercepted, it is turned into unreadable ciphertext and cannot be understood without the key, protecting its confidentiality.
points: data is scrambled into ciphertext / unreadable
intercepted data cannot be understood without the key
